note: Planting directions from Iowa State University Extension 'Planting and harvesting times for garden vegetables' (PM 534, central Iowa; southern Iowa ~1 week earlier, northern ~1 week later).

rows.Radish: several plantings 7–10 days apart in spring; fall plantings mid-August to mid-September
rows.Lettuce: sow in early spring; fall plantings in August
rows.Onions: dry onions: sow seeds early to mid April; sets and plants early April to May 1
rows.Peas: sow in early spring as soon as the soil can be worked; fall planting about August 1–10
rows.Spinach: sow in April; fall crop about August 10
rows.Cabbages: transplants early April to May 1; direct seed in summer for a fall crop
rows.Collards and kale: seed with lettuce and other early spring crops; direct-seed early July for a fall crop
rows.Turnips: sow in April and again in August or early September
rows.Snap beans: any time after May 5; last practical date August 1
rows.Sweet corn: when soil reaches 60°F; last practical date for an early variety July 1
rows.Tomatoes: seedlings mid-May; last practical date June 20
rows.Peppers and eggplants: seedlings mid-May; last practical date June 20
rows.Summer squashes: seed mid-May; last practical date July 20
rows.Cucumbers: seed mid-May; last practical date July 20
rows.Muskmelons: seed mid-May; last practical date June 20
rows.Watermelons: seed mid-May; last practical date June 20
